title: Prepare, operate and maintain a tractor in a non-production situation

lessons.title: Knowing the tractor
lessons.html:
Tractors on farms and plantations

Tractors pull trailers of timber, poles and feed, and work implements such as slashers and rippers. This unit is about driving a tractor safely in a non-production situation: moving it around the yard and on roads, without working an implement in production. Only trained and authorised drivers may operate a tractor.

Main parts and controls

Part or controlWhat it does
EngineUsually diesel; gives power
Clutch pedalDisconnects the engine from the wheels to change gear or stop
Brake pedalsLeft and right brakes; lock them together for road driving
Gear lever and range leverSelect speed and direction
Hand throttle and foot throttleControl engine speed
Parking brakeHolds the tractor when parked
Three-point linkage and hydraulic leverLift and lower implements
PTO leverDrives implements; keep off when not in use
Differential lockLocks the rear wheels together for grip; never use when turning
InstrumentsOil pressure, temperature, charging, fuel, hour meter
ROPS and seat beltRoll-over protection; always wear the belt when the ROPS is up

The biggest dangers

  • Roll-overs: on slopes, ditches, river banks, and when turning too fast. Always use the ROPS and seat belt.
  • Run-overs: people falling off or being run over. Never carry passengers unless there is a proper passenger seat.
  • PTO entanglement: loose clothing caught in a turning shaft.
  • Starting in gear: never start the tractor from the ground beside the wheels.

Read the operator's manual for your tractor. Each model has its own controls and warnings.

lessons.title: Preparing and starting the tractor
lessons.html:
Daily pre-start checks

Do these with the engine off, on level ground. Use the checklist your workplace gives you and sign it.

Walk-around

  • Look for leaks of oil, fuel, coolant or hydraulic oil under and around the tractor.
  • Tyres: pressure looks right, no cuts or bulges, wheel nuts tight.
  • ROPS and seat belt in good condition.
  • Lights, indicators, mirrors, reflectors and slow-moving vehicle sign clean and working.
  • PTO guard in place.
  • Steps and platform clean; no tools or loose objects in the cab.

Fluid checks

  • Engine oil on the dipstick between the marks.
  • Coolant level in the reservoir (check only when cool).
  • Hydraulic and transmission oil level.
  • Fuel. Refuel with the engine off, no smoking.
  • Air filter: empty the dust bowl or check the indicator.
  • Grease the daily grease points as the manual shows.
  • Battery terminals clean and tight.

Getting on and starting

  1. Climb on facing the tractor, using the steps and handholds (three points of contact).
  2. Adjust the seat and fasten the seat belt.
  3. Check the parking brake is on, gears in neutral, PTO off, hydraulic lever down.
  4. Press the clutch if the tractor requires it.
  5. Turn the key. Use the cold-start aid only as the manual says.
  6. Check that the oil pressure and charging lights go out. If the oil light stays on, switch off at once and report.
  7. Let the engine warm up at low speed for a short time.

If any check shows a fault that affects safety, such as a flat tyre, leaking brake fluid or a broken seat belt, do not use the tractor. Tag it and tell your supervisor.

Never start a tractor in a closed shed without ventilation. Diesel exhaust is dangerous.

lessons.title: Driving, parking and after-use care
lessons.html:
Driving safely

  • Look all around, sound the hooter and check no one is near before moving.
  • Choose a low gear and release the clutch smoothly.
  • Drive at a speed that suits the ground. Slow down on rough roads, in the yard and near people.
  • Lock the brake pedals together before driving on roads or at speed.
  • On slopes, drive straight up and down, not across. Go down in a low gear; never coast in neutral or with the clutch pressed.
  • Keep away from the edges of ditches, dams and river banks.
  • Turn slowly. Never use the diff lock when turning.
  • Look behind before reversing.
  • Keep both hands on the wheel. No cell phone use while driving.
  • On public roads, obey traffic rules, use lights and pull over to let traffic pass where safe.

Parking and shut-down

  1. Park on level, firm ground, away from traffic and not on slopes if possible.
  2. Lower any implement or loader to the ground.
  3. Put the gears in neutral and apply the parking brake.
  4. Switch off the PTO.
  5. Let the engine idle for a short time to cool, especially a turbo engine, then switch off.
  6. Remove the key.
  7. Climb down facing the tractor, using three points of contact. Never jump.

Care after use

  • Clean mud, grass and debris from the radiator, engine area and steps.
  • Check for new leaks or damage.
  • Refuel at the end of the day if the farm prefers, to reduce condensation in the tank.
  • Write the hours and any faults on the logbook or checklist.
  • Report faults; do not use a tractor with faulty brakes, steering or lights.
  • Service at the hours the manual and workshop schedule say.

Key points

  • Always wear the seat belt with the ROPS up; never carry passengers without a seat.
  • Do the pre-start checks and sign the checklist.
  • Start only from the seat, in neutral, with the PTO off.
  • Drive straight up and down slopes, lock the brakes together on roads.
  • Park with implements down, parking brake on and key removed.
